question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Bombay — Location / Acquisition]
options: Bombay — A natural harbour island on India's western coast
Bombay — Received by England as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry in 1661
Bombay — Located on the Coromandel (eastern) coast of India
Bombay — Transferred from the Crown to the English East India Company in 1668
wrong_fact: Bombay is on India's western coast (Konkan / Arabian Sea), NOT on the Coromandel (eastern) coast.
explanation: Bombay (Mumbai) is an island city situated on the western coast of India, facing the Arabian Sea. It was part of Portugal's dowry to England when King Charles II married Catherine of Braganza in 1661. In 1668, Charles II leased Bombay to the English East India Company for a nominal rent. The Coromandel coast is on the southeastern side of India (modern Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh), where cities like Madras and Masulipatnam are located.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Bombay — Key Person / Development]
options: Gerald Aungier — Governor of Bombay who developed it into a thriving commercial city (1669–1677)
Bombay — Replaced Surat as the English western-coast headquarters in 1687
Child's War (1686–90) — Conflict that temporarily cost the English their Bombay settlement
Sir Josiah Child — Promoted aggressive expansion policy that led to the disastrous war with Aurangzeb
wrong_fact: Child's War (1686–90) did NOT cause the English to lose Bombay permanently. The Mughals expelled the English from their Bengal and Surat factories, not Bombay. The English were briefly humiliated but Bombay itself was not captured.
explanation: Child's War refers to the Anglo-Mughal War of 1686–90, triggered by Sir Josiah Child's aggressive policy. Aurangzeb's forces expelled the English from Surat and Bengal factories, but Bombay — being an island — was not captured. The English were humbled and had to seek pardon from Aurangzeb. Gerald Aungier (Governor 1669–77) transformed Bombay with civic institutions, courts, a mint, and population growth. The English presidency was formally moved from Surat to Bombay in 1687.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Bombay — Portuguese & Mughal Context]
options: Bombay — Originally a Portuguese possession called 'Bom Bahia' (Good Bay)
Bombay — Seven islands that were gradually reclaimed and connected into one landmass
Bombay — Ceded to England by Portugal via the Treaty of Madras (1660)
Bombay — Became the capital of the Bombay Presidency under British India
wrong_fact: Bombay was NOT ceded via the Treaty of Madras. It was transferred as a royal marriage dowry under the Treaty of Whitehall / marriage treaty of 1661 when Charles II married Catherine of Braganza.
explanation: The Treaty of Madras (1661) was a separate agreement between the English and the Bijapur Sultanate relating to English rights at Madras — it had nothing to do with Bombay. Bombay passed from Portugal to England through the marriage treaty between Charles II and Catherine of Braganza in 1661. The name 'Bom Bahia' (Portuguese for 'Good Bay') was anglicised to 'Bombay.' The original settlement comprised seven islands that were gradually interconnected through land reclamation projects. It later became the seat of the Bombay Presidency.
